steps.title: Reading more than one sentence at a time
body: Every text you've read so far has been one sentence. A paragraph is several sentences working together — and the connectors you just learned (أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ، أَثْنَاءَ، أَخِيرًا، ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ، بَيْنَمَا، فَجْأَةً، طَبْعًا) are what tell you the order events happened in, not just that they happened.

Reading for comprehension means holding the whole passage in mind, not just the sentence in front of you — a question might ask what happened first, what happened while something else was going on, or what the paragraph is mainly about.

steps.title: Two short paragraphs
steps.intro: Read each paragraph sentence by sentence. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: The main idea
steps.prompt: What is the first paragraph mainly about?
steps.explanation: The paragraph follows one connected event — buying a ticket, traveling, reading on the way, arriving, and returning home — all part of one trip.

steps.title: Tracking the details
steps.prompt: According to the paragraph, what did the student do أَثْنَاءَ (during) the trip?
steps.explanation: Buying the ticket happened first (أَوَّلًا) and returning home happened last (أَخِيرًا) — reading the book is specifically what أَثْنَاءَ الرِّحْلَة (during the trip) describes.

steps.title: What happened while...
steps.prompt: What happened بَيْنَمَا (while) the man was in the garden?

options.label: He suddenly saw a plane in the sky
He went to buy a ticket

steps.explanation: The second paragraph's event is the plane in the sky — the ticket-buying belongs to the first paragraph, not this one.

steps.title: You've read your first connected paragraphs
steps.message: Two short stories, eight new connectors put to work, and a first look at reading for the main idea instead of just word-by-word. Fully-vowelled paragraphs like these are exactly what real Arabic reading looks like next.
